vulnerability_patterns.description: A size check validated only the starting offset, not the full width of a subsequent 4-byte read, allowing reads beyond the section buffer end.
trigger_conditions: `name` length and alignment produce a `crc_offset` that is less than the section size but greater than `section_size - 4`
Execution reaches `bfd_get_32 (abfd, contents + crc_offset)` with insufficient remaining bytes in the section buffer
fix_patterns: Replace start-offset-only validation with width-aware bounds check for the exact read size
Guard `offset + read_width > buffer_size` before dereferencing or decoding multi-byte values
evidence_lines: Comment states intent: `avoid reading off the end of the buffer.`

entry_points: Call sites computing offsets from `strnlen(...)`, alignment arithmetic, or section-size-derived bounds
suggestions: Prefer sink-aware checks that compare `offset + access_width` against authoritative buffer length, not just `offset < size`.
Model decoder helpers like `bfd_get_32` as fixed-width reads requiring 4 available bytes.
Track transformations such as `strnlen(...) + 1` and alignment rounding `(x + 3) & ~3` because they can move an offset from safe to near-end positions.
Prefer missing full-span validation over plain null-check reasoning.
Flag cases where a buffer length from `bfd_get_section_size` is reused for string scanning and then for later structured reads without revalidating the read width.

shared_analysis.analysis_rationale: The patch tightens the bounds check in `bfd_get_section_size` usage before reading a 4-byte CRC from `contents + crc_offset`. Previously it only rejected `crc_offset >= bfd_get_section_size (sect)`, which still allowed `crc_offset` values near the end of the section where `bfd_get_32 (abfd, contents + crc_offset)` would read past the buffer. The fix changes this to `if (crc_offset + 4 > bfd_get_section_size (sect)) return NULL;`, directly guarding the full 4-byte read width.
